requirements.judgement: Ore mixture, oxide compound and metal species distinguished: concentrating 200 kg to 100 kg retains 40 kg oxide, changing 20% to 40% without making iron; independent 150−60=90 kg and 30/90=one third practice.
Native gold grains already contain uncombined element; physical collection versus oxide reduction contrasted. Often-native tendency does not exclude compound occurrences or contamination.
Physical removal of iron-free rock leaves iron chemically combined in oxide. Increased oxide fraction is neither elemental-metal yield nor chemical reduction.
Carbon school position below Al and above Fe supports suitable oxide method selection, not an unconditional industrial route for every compound.
Actual Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂ independently conserves Fe2/C3/O6; iron oxide loses oxygen and CO gains it. Carbon-based route distinguished from CO product confusion.
Aluminium above carbon uses electrolysis of alumina in the appropriate molten bath; simple carbon heating and ordinary aqueous-salt deposition explicitly not substituted.

Mobile electrolyte ions versus external electrons and negative cathode electron gain distinguished. Actual doubled half-equation +6−6=0 conserves Al2; carbon anode conductance/consumption does not reclassify the method.
Suitable compound and process conditions retained; fixed solid ions and competing aqueous water reactions limit transfer. Balanced formula alone is not evidence of a viable route.
Interpret supplied starting oxide, physical separation, metal-forming step and inputs without requiring a factory recipe; iron-free remainder assumption prevents hidden metal-content inference.

Recommendation names product quality, waste composition/treatment and energy source with comparable boundaries. Current alone does not prove carbon footprint, and unrecovered iron need not be elemental metal waste.

Copper heat-exchanger thermal transfer and plumbing workability/conditional corrosion resistance distinguish actual use benefits from immunity claims.
Suitable soft iron magnetizes readily and releases much magnetization after field removal for a switched electromagnet; pure iron and all steel grades not interchangeable.

Stainless chromium supports a chromium-rich oxide layer and conditional cutlery/sink corrosion resistance; neither a pure-chromium coating nor immunity asserted.

Grade/treatment restrictions retained; nickel-free and magnetic stainless possibilities defeat blanket identification rules. All three named steel types are taught, not new compulsory grade thresholds.
Alloy defined as metal plus one or more elements; iron/carbon qualifies despite non-metal carbon, and exactly-two-metals definition rejected.
Different supplied steel percentages remain variable alloy mixtures, not one fixed compound formula. Two-element and three-element bookkeeping assumptions stated.
